quote: We may hope that machines will eventually compete with men in all purely intellectual fields. But which are the best ones to start with? Even this is a difficult decision... We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan M. Turing
context: From the concluding section of Computing Machinery and Intelligence, defining the roadmap toward trainable artificial minds.

quote: The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point. Frequently the messages have meaning... these semantic aspects of communication are irrelevant to the engineering problem.
author: Claude E. Shannon
context: The opening thesis of A Mathematical Theory of Communication, which laid the mathematical groundwork for digital computing, entropy, and statistical learning.

quote: The study is to proceed on the basis of the conjecture that every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.
author: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester & Claude Shannon
context: The 1955 workshop proposal that formally christened the field of Artificial Intelligence at Dartmouth College.
paper_title: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence

quote: The representation of concepts by patterns of activity over many units allows the network to generalize to new cases in a natural way... and generalized backpropagation provides the credit-assignment mechanism required to learn internal representations.
author: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton & Ronald Williams
context: Published in Nature, demonstrating that multi-layer neural networks can learn arbitrary non-linear mappings via gradient descent.

quote: We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output... Attention is all you need.
author: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, et al.
context: The seminal NeurIPS 2017 paper that replaced recurrent neural networks with self-attention, establishing the backbone for all modern LLMs.

quote: Scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, demonstrating that massive autoregressive pretraining allows models to perform diverse tasks with zero gradient updates.
author: Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder, et al.
context: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, introducing GPT-3 (175B parameters) and proving scaling laws produce emergent few-shot capabilities.

quote: While reasoning traces help models induce, track, and update action plans, action execution interfaces with external knowledge sources. Synergizing reasoning and acting creates agents that think, act, and observe in closed loops.
author: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, et al.
context: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models, establishing the architecture that powers modern autonomous agent frameworks.
paper_title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

quote: Large-scale reinforcement learning applied directly to base models without supervised cold-start data demonstrates that reasoning capabilities can emerge purely through autonomous exploration, self-verification, and reward incentives.
author: DeepSeek-AI
context: DeepSeek-R1, demonstrating that pure RL elicits long-chain reasoning, self-correction, and reflective thought without human demonstration data.
paper_title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
